about: Homework for this pillar, one list per AI (Claude writes it; tools/kit/render.py in jpavia10/prometheus-hub turns it into docs/agents/QUEUE_{ai}.md and the Drive docs). Every task says exactly what to read, what to make, how many, where to save it, how Claude checks it and what makes it not done. A task is done only when the file passes the checks, never because it was sent.

tasks.title: Kairos Meridian: the spec sheet (time: Google Calendar, deadlines from every pillar (homework due dates, bills from Midas), the shape of the day)
tasks.why: Kairos Meridian is a seat on the desk with no page yet. Joseph wants each pillar developed on its own; the first step is a spec Claude can build from.
steps: Write the spec for Kairos Meridian: time: Google Calendar, deadlines from every pillar (homework due dates, bills from Midas), the shape of the day.
At least 6 data sources with their real API names and documentation URLs (open each one); say plainly when something has no public API.
Four first screens, each listing every number on it and where it comes from.
Five 'done when' checks that can be tested on a phone.
Event titles stay in Joseph's calendar; the page reads them live.

deliver.shape: one markdown file with these 6 headings, in this order: 1 Purpose (one sentence) | 2 Data sources (a table: source | what it gives | how to get it (API name) | docs URL | sign-in type | cost | limits) | 3 First four screens (for each: its name, every number and list on it, where each comes from) | 4 Version 1 done when (5 checks Claude can test) | 5 Privacy (what never leaves the device) | 6 What Joseph must do once (accounts, keys, apps)

tasks.done_when: All 6 headings, at least 6 sources with working docs URLs, 4 screens, 5 testable checks.
checks: Claude checks each 'done when' can be tested without asking Joseph.
rejected_if: a row copied from another row with the names changed
a source URL that does not open or does not say what the row claims
fewer items than the count
a file saved anywhere but the folder named here, or under another name
an API that does not exist or a docs URL for something else
a screen that lists a number with no source

tasks.title: Fixed dates 2026-2028: federal holidays, tax deadlines, clock changes
tasks.why: Kairos shows the day; these dates must be on it without anyone typing them.
steps: US federal holidays 2026, 2027, 2028 with the observed date (opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/pay-leave/federal-holidays/).
IRS individual deadlines 2026 and 2027 (filing day, the four estimated-tax days, extension day) from irs.gov.
US daylight-saving start and end 2026-2028 (nist.gov or timeanddate.com).
One row per date with the source URL and quote.
tasks.done_when: At least 55 rows (33 holidays, 12 tax days, 6 clock changes), every date quoted.
checks: Claude checks every holiday against OPM and every tax day against IRS.
rejected_if: fewer rows than the count, or a row missing a field of the shape
a row copied from another row with the names changed
a URL that does not open, is a front page or a search page, or does not say what the row claims
a quote that is not on the page it cites (Claude opens 10 rows at random)
a file saved anywhere but the folder named here, or under another name
a date from a calendar-app blog

tasks.title: 20 focus methods with their exact timing rules and primary source
tasks.why: Kairos's focus clock offers methods; each needs its real rules (minutes, breaks, cycles), not a blog summary.
steps: 20 methods (Pomodoro, 52/17, ultradian 90/20, time-boxing, Flowtime, timeblocking, Eat the Frog, 1-3-5, ...).

For each: work minutes, short break, long break, cycles before the long break (null when the method has none), and the primary source: the creator's book with page, the creator's own site, or a paper's DOI.
tasks.done_when: 20 methods, timing traceable to the source.
rejected_if: fewer rows than the count, or a row missing a field of the shape
a row copied from another row with the names changed
a URL that does not open, is a front page or a search page, or does not say what the row claims
a quote that is not on the page it cites (Claude opens 10 rows at random)
a file saved anywhere but the folder named here, or under another name
a method whose only source is a listicle

tasks.title: An ICS test file with 40 made-up events that cover every hard case
tasks.why: Kairos will import calendars; Claude needs a file that breaks weak parsers.
steps: Write one valid iCalendar file (RFC 5545) with 40 VEVENTs: 5 all-day, 3 multi-day, 6 weekly RRULE (with BYDAY), 4 monthly RRULE (BYMONTHDAY and BYSETPOS), 3 with EXDATE, 3 in America/Los_Angeles, 3 in Europe/London, 3 in Asia/Tokyo (with VTIMEZONE blocks), 2 across the 2026-03-08 and 2026-11-01 US clock changes, 4 overlapping, 2 crossing midnight, 2 with a 0-minute duration.
Put the case name in each SUMMARY (e.g. 'weekly MO,WE,FR until 2026-12-31').
tasks.done_when: One file that a strict parser (python icalendar) reads with no error, 40 events, every case present.
checks: Claude parses it and expands the rules for Nov 2026 - Mar 2027.
rejected_if: fewer rows than the count, or a row missing a field of the shape
a row copied from another row with the names changed
a URL that does not open, is a front page or a search page, or does not say what the row claims
a quote that is not on the page it cites (Claude opens 10 rows at random)
a file saved anywhere but the folder named here, or under another name
a file that does not parse
a case missing from the list

tasks.title: Google Calendar Events resource: the 30 fields Kairos v2 reads
tasks.why: For version 2 (Google Calendar sync), Claude needs the exact field names and types.
steps: From developers.google.com/calendar/api/v3/reference/events list 30 fields (id, summary, start.dateTime, start.date, start.timeZone, end..., recurrence, recurringEventId, status, transparency, attendees[].responseStatus, reminders.overrides[], ...).
For each: exact path, type, writable or not, and the meaning quoted.
checks: Claude compares with the reference page.

tasks.title: Kairos Meridian: second reader on Gemini's spec
tasks.why: Every source in a spec gets a second reader before Claude builds on it.
inputs: Gemini's file kairos_gemini_spec_*.md in the incoming folder (once it is there)
steps: Open every data source's docs URL; for each write: source, Gemini's claim (sign-in, cost, limits), what the page says, agree/differ.
Add up to 5 sources Gemini missed, same columns.

deliver.shape: table: source | gemini says | page says | url | agree/differ
